method: Re-read real code: getCUCount() (LibraryIO.py:686-702). NOTE line 701 is the SECOND `if CU is None:` (the first is line 689, immediately after CU=os.environ.get('CU',None)). At line 701 CU is NOT purely env-derived: lines 689-699 may repopulate CU from the rocminfo subprocess. The claim's pure_helper cu_is_none(cu_env) models only the env read, so it is an incomplete model of line 701. Verified the witnesses anyway by faithfully re-executing lines 688-701 in-container (docker exec, env injected via os.environ, rocminfo stdout injected as bytes). TRUE example (env CU unset, rocminfo_output=='') -> CU is None == True (reproduced). FALSE example (env CU=='64') -> CU is None == False (reproduced). Both claimed witnesses reproduce against the REAL line-701 logic. The TRUE witness survives at line 701 precisely because it pins rocminfo_output=='' (empty -> regex match fails -> CU stays None). Adversarial probe (env unset + rocminfo_output=='Compute Unit: 64') yields line701==False, which the env-only helper would mis-predict as True -- a modeling imprecision, not a witness failure. Both polarities reachable; classification solver-backed-under-assumptions is correct (predicate controlled by OS env + subprocess, not constant-foldable). Confirmed SAT without upgrade or downgrade.
caveats: pure_helper/note describe line 701 but actually model line-689 (env-only) semantics; line 701 also depends on the rocminfo subprocess.
TRUE witness is valid for line 701 only because rocminfo_output is pinned empty (parse fails). If rocminfo parses a CU count, line 701 is False even with env unset.
CrossHair pass on the helper is NOT a proof and does not cover the subprocess-repopulation path.
